claims.text: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), each Theorem 5.4 Schur generating set has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements; the paper reports verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1382:   Given a bigrassmannian $v=v_{r,s,t,n}$ in type $A_{n-1}$ with $\schubp_v = s_{i^j}$, let
1383: $$
1384: \begin{aligned}
1385: a&:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\\
1386: b&:=\min(i,j).
1387: \end{aligned}
1388: $$
1389: 
1390: Then $J_v$ is generated as an ideal of 
1391: $H^{\star}(G/P_J, {\mathbb Z})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$ by 
1392: \begin{equation}
1393: \label{generating-set-one}
1394: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}) \}.
1395: \end{equation}
1396: 
1397: Alternatively, $J_v$ is generated by 
1398: \begin{equation}
1399: \label{generating-set-two}
1400: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (i^j,b^a) \}.
1401: \end{equation}
1402: \end{theorem}
1403: 
1404: We delay our proof of Theorem~\ref{J-generators} until Section~\ref{minconjsection}.
1405: 
1406: \noindent
1407: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets \eqref{generating-set-one} and \eqref{generating-set-two} for $J_v$,
1408: the shapes $\mu$ indexing the generators $s_\mu$ run through an interval between
1409: the $j \times i$ rectangular shape $i^j$ and the disjoint union of $i^j$ with a 
1410: smaller rectangle of shape $a \times b$ or $b \times a$. 
1411: In \eqref{generating-set-one} the smaller rectangle is to the right
1412: of the rectangle $i^j$, with both top-justified, while in \eqref{generating-set-two} the 
1413: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle $i^j$, with both left-justified.  
1414: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size $\binom{a+b}{a}$
1415: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
1416: have generating function 
1417: $$
1418: \sum_\mu q^{|\mu|} = q^{ij} \qbin{a+b}{a},
1419: $$
1420: where $\qbin{a+b}{a}$ is a $q$-{\it binomial coefficient} or {\it Gaussian polynomial} 
1421: \cite[I.2 Exer. 3]{Macdonald}.

claims.text: For the in-box case \((r,n-r,i,j)=(4,5,2,2)\), \(a=b=2\), \(N=6\), and the computed \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) has rank \(6\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=6=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]

For the first \(r\)-boundary case outside the reported box, \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,1,1,1)\), \(a=0,b=1,N=1\); \(Q\) has rank \(1\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=1=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]

For the nontrivial outside-\(r\) case \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,2,1,1)\), \(a=b=1,N=2\); \(Q\) has rank \(2\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=2=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]

For the first \(n-r\)-boundary case outside the reported box, \((r,n-r,i,j)=(1,6,1,1)\), \(a=0,b=1,N=1\); \(Q\) has rank \(1\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=1=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]
These finite torsion-free examples support, but do not prove, \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) or \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\) in all admissible cases.
